summary: The flake did not measurably change between day 1 and day 2. The raw peak positions differ by about +2.5 cm-1, but the Si substrate line moved by the same amount (519.98 to 522.47 cm-1), so the spectrometer calibration drifted between days. After Si correction, the E2g1-like band (384.05 vs 384.07 cm-1), the A1g-like band (405.61 vs 405.54 cm-1), their separation (21.56 vs 21.47 cm-1), their widths and their relative intensity are all unchanged within errors. The separation of 21.5 cm-1 points to bilayer (2L) on the Lee et al. 2010 table. Nothing supports the colleague's adsorbate doping or strain hypothesis at the sensitivity of these spectra. The only real day-to-day differences are instrumental: a higher background (about +120 counts) and a different spectral sampling (0.53 vs 0.66 cm-1 per point).

observations.finding: Si reference line shifted by +2.49 cm-1 between days, so the apparent sample shift is calibration.
observations.evidence: Si line 519.98 +/- 0.02 cm-1 on day 1 (offset -0.72 from 520.7) vs 522.47 +/- 0.03 cm-1 on day 2 (offset +1.77); difference +2.49 cm-1 (rl_qc.py, rl_fit.py). Raw E' 383.33 -> 385.83 (+2.51) and A1' 404.88 -> 407.31 (+2.43), i.e. the same rigid shift as the Si line.

observations.finding: After Si correction, neither mode shifts between days within fit errors.
observations.evidence: rl_series.py --si-correct: E'-like 384.05 +/- 0.01 (day 1) vs 384.07 +/- 0.02 (day 2), shift +0.02 +/- 0.03 cm-1. A1'-like 405.61 +/- 0.07 vs 405.54 +/- 0.10, shift -0.07 +/- 0.12 cm-1. Series plot right panel shows both shifts consistent with zero.

observations.finding: The calibration-independent separation is unchanged, and it identifies a bilayer.
observations.evidence: omega(A1g-like) - omega(E2g1-like) = 21.56 +/- 0.07 cm-1 (day 1) vs 21.47 +/- 0.11 cm-1 (day 2); difference -0.09 +/- 0.13 cm-1. Relation mos2_layer_number_from_separation gives 2L (confidence high) using the Lee 2010 table (1L 19.1, 2L 21.4, 3L 23.1, 4L 24.3, bulk 25.2 cm-1). Same result on both days.
observations.source: Lee, Yan, Brus, Heinz, Hone, Ryu 2010, ACS Nano 4, 2695, doi:10.1021/nn1003937, arXiv:1005.2509, Fig. 2b (via rl.py apply_relation)

observations.finding: Linewidths are unchanged, so no broadening signature of doping or defect change.
observations.evidence: E'-like FWHM 2.08 +/- 0.06 (day 1) vs 2.14 +/- 0.19 cm-1 (day 2); A1'-like FWHM 6.13 +/- 0.26 vs 6.22 +/- 0.42 cm-1. Both are within the 1 to 2 sigma errors of each other.

observations.finding: Relative band intensities are unchanged within errors.
observations.evidence: A1'-like/E'-like peak height ratio 0.335 (day 1) vs 0.334 (day 2). E'-like height relative to Si 0.965 vs 0.946 (about -2%), but day 2 height error is about 6%, so the change is not significant. Integrated-area ratio 0.986 vs 0.971 (not significant without area errors).

observations.finding: Day 2 background is higher, and peak positions and heights relative to Si are not affected by it.
observations.evidence: Mean counts 150 to 200 cm-1: 343 (day 1) vs 477 (day 2); 550 to 600 cm-1: 373 vs 482; the increase is roughly flat, about +120 to +130 counts (about +35%). Si peak height 908 vs 907 counts. Cause not identified (ambient light, dark or integration settings, or photoluminescence).

observations.finding: Acquisition settings differ between days, which is a measurement-setup change.
observations.evidence: Point spacing 0.53 cm-1 (day 1) vs 0.66 cm-1 (day 2); strongest-band SNR 68 vs 57; point counts 949 vs 756. Both spectra cover 150 to 649.6 cm-1.

observations.finding: No defect-activated LA(M) band (about 227 cm-1) is detected above noise in either spectrum.
observations.evidence: Mean counts in windows around 227 cm-1 are at background level on both days (day 1 345.8, day 2 489.3, background ranges 343 to 355 and 477 to 499). No spike and no peak was fitted there. Absence is weak evidence at SNR 57 to 68 on the main peak.
observations.source: Mignuzzi et al. 2015, PRB 91, 195411 (LA(M) as defect band, as cited in materials/MoS2.md)

observations.finding: The top library match is spurious (it matches the Si line), so the identification rests on the MoS2 literature entry, not the match score.
observations.evidence: rl.py match_library ranks HSi first (score 0.62, matched only the 520 cm-1 line), MoS2 CRD entry second (0.56, E and A1 matched), but the 2H-MoS2 literature table is the physically sensible reference.

observations.finding: Absolute positions after Si correction sit about 0.7 to 0.8 cm-1 above Lee 2010's 2L values, and both modes move the same way. This points to calibration, not to doping or strain.
observations.evidence: Corrected E'-like 384.05 vs Lee 2L 383.4 cm-1 (+0.65); A1'-like 405.61 vs 404.8 (+0.8). Lee's Fig. 2b values are read to about +/-0.3 cm-1. Doping (A1' led) and strain (E' led, with splitting) would not move both modes together.
observations.source: Lee et al. 2010, arXiv:1005.2509, Fig. 2b; Conley et al. 2013, arXiv:1305.3880; Chakraborty et al. 2012, arXiv:1206.1758 (as summarized in reference/materials/MoS2.md)

properties.name: layers
properties.source: Lee et al. 2010, ACS Nano 4, 2695, arXiv:1005.2509, Fig. 2b; relation mos2_layer_number_from_separation with separation 21.56 +/- 0.07 cm-1 (day 1) and 21.47 +/- 0.11 cm-1 (day 2); same answer on both days

properties.name: defect_level
properties.value: none detected (low confidence, limited by SNR and no LA(M) fit)

properties.name: strain_sign
properties.source: E'-like shift +0.02 +/- 0.03 cm-1 after Si correction; Conley et al. 2013, arXiv:1305.3880 (1L coefficient about -4.5 cm-1/% uniaxial, indicative only for this flake)

properties.name: doping_type
properties.source: A1'-like shift -0.07 +/- 0.12 cm-1 with unchanged width; Chakraborty et al. 2012, arXiv:1206.1758 (1L A1g softens about 4 cm-1 at 1.8e13 cm-2, so 1L order-of-magnitude bound about 1e12 cm-2)

properties.name: phase
properties.value: 2H (as stated by the user; E/A pair with 21.5 cm-1 separation is consistent with 2H bilayer)
properties.source: Lee et al. 2010, arXiv:1005.2509 (bulk D6h labels, used for all layer numbers); user-stated material

caveats: Si correction assumes the Si line in each spectrum tracks the sample's spectrometer offset; a 2.5 cm-1 drift in one day is large and was not explained, so the cause (grating move, recalibration, or a changed range/sampling) should be checked. The separation metric avoids this assumption and gives the same answer.

Fit errors are statistical only; calibration scatter (typically a few tenths of a cm-1) is not included in the position errors, so the shift bounds below are conservative in intent but not formal 2-sigma calibrated limits.

Relation bounds: an A1' shift of about -0.3 cm-1 (2-sigma) corresponds to roughly 1e12 cm-2 electron doping using the 1L Chakraborty coefficient; an E' shift below about 0.1 cm-1 corresponds to strain well below 0.1 % using the 1L Conley coefficient. Both coefficients are for monolayers, so they are indicative only for this bilayer-like flake.

Laser power at the sample, focus and temperature were not reported for either day. A power or heating difference would redshift both modes and could be masked by the calibration shift; the 2-sigma shift bound is the only thing ruling it out here.

The Lee 2010 separation table was measured at 2.7 cm-1 resolution and read from a figure (about +/-0.3 cm-1). Layers 2 and 3 differ by 1.7 cm-1 in separation, which is robust against the 0.07 to 0.11 cm-1 fit error but not against a systematic resolution or substrate effect.
Adsorbate doping is not directly constrained: the A1' shift is only a proxy, and the 1L-based coefficients cannot be converted to an ambient-adsorbate doping level for this sample.
Background, sampling and the Si line position all changed between days; the setup is not identical, so the comparison is between two configurations, not two identical measurements.
Same-spot identity was not verified (no map, optical image or position log), and no polarization geometry was given.
questions_for_user: Why did the Si reference line move by 2.5 cm-1 between days (grating move, recalibration, different spectral window)? The day 2 point spacing is also 0.66 vs 0.53 cm-1, so the settings changed.

Was the laser power at the sample, the objective, the integration time and the number of accumulations the same on both days? Was the day 2 background increase (about +35%) from room light, dark counts, a longer integration, or photoluminescence?
Was the same spot confirmed on both days (optical image, stage coordinates, or a mapping reference)?

Were there any scans or laser exposures on this spot between day 1 and day 2, and what was the temperature? Previous laser exposure in air can change A1g and E2g1 by about 1 cm-1 (Bera et al. 2017, arXiv:1707.09386).
Is the layer number independently confirmed (optical contrast, AFM, or a low-frequency shear/breathing measurement)? The 150 cm-1 cutoff means the interlayer modes are not in these spectra.
citations: Lee, Yan, Brus, Heinz, Hone, Ryu 2010, ACS Nano 4, 2695, doi:10.1021/nn1003937, arXiv:1005.2509, Fig. 2b (514.5 nm, E2g1/A1g positions and separation vs layer number; 1L 19.1, 2L 21.4, 3L 23.1, 4L 24.3, bulk 25.2 cm-1)
Conley et al. 2013, Nano Lett. 13, 3626, arXiv:1305.3880 (uniaxial strain: E' about -4.5 cm-1/%, 1L)
Chakraborty et al. 2012, PRB 85, 161403, arXiv:1206.1758 (electron doping: 1L A1g softens about 4 cm-1 at 1.8e13 cm-2)
Bera et al. 2017, arXiv:1707.09386 (laser exposure in air hardens A1g by 1.4 cm-1 and softens E2g1 by 1 cm-1)
Mignuzzi et al. 2015, PRB 91, 195411 (LA(M) near 227 cm-1 as the defect-activated band)
Buscema et al. 2014, arXiv:1311.3869 (A1g vs substrate doping, separation robust across substrates)
reference/materials/MoS2.md, sections Thickness, Strain and doping, Defects and quality, Temperature and heating, Pitfalls (summaries of the above and of Zhang X. et al. 2015, arXiv:1502.00701)
limits: The data cannot separate a few-tenths-cm-1 doping or strain change from calibration drift with a single-day Si reference, unless the Si line is trusted to track the sample.
No polarization geometry, temperature log, laser power or spot verification were available; these would be needed to rule out heating or a different spot.
Low-frequency modes (shear, breathing) lie outside the 150 cm-1 window, so they cannot independently confirm the layer count.
Doping and strain bounds rely on monolayer coefficients (Chakraborty 2012; Conley 2013) and are indicative only for this flake.
The Lee 2010 table was read from a figure, so layer assignments carry about +/-0.3 cm-1 systematic uncertainty.
rl_qc.py found no spikes and no saturation in either spectrum; the matcher's top hit (HSi) was rejected as spurious.
